title: The tools of good works (ch. 4)
hook: a list including keep death daily before your eyes and never despair of God's mercy

segments.voice: Yesterday, taking counsel: the abbot calls the whole community, because the Lord often shows what is better to the younger. Your line was the youngest may be right. Whose view did you ask? Day one thousand one hundred ninety-one.

A pegboard on a garage wall. Each tool hangs on its own hook, with its outline drawn around it in marker, so you can see at a glance what's missing. Hammer. Level. The good screwdriver somebody borrowed. Nobody uses every tool every day. You grab the one the job needs. Chapter four of Saint Benedict's Rule is a pegboard like that, for the inner life. A long list, hung up in plain sight. Today: the tools of good works.
screen: `A PEGBOARD IN A GARAGE.` → `GRAB THE ONE THE JOB NEEDS.` → `A PEGBOARD FOR THE SOUL.`

segments.voice: Benedict doesn't explain the tools. He just lists them, one short line after another. The first is the great commandment. Jesus gives it in the Douay-Rheims: "Thou shalt love the Lord thy God with thy whole heart, and with thy whole soul, and with thy whole mind." Then, love your neighbor as yourself. After that the list runs on, some of it from the Ten Commandments, some of it from the Sermon on the Mount, some of it Benedict's own. Prefer nothing to the love of Christ. Don't give a false peace. Make peace with someone you've quarreled with before the sun goes down. Pray for your enemies. And then two that stop people. Keep death daily before your eyes. That sounds grim, but in the Rule it isn't meant to frighten. It's meant to focus: if today could be the last, what actually matters? And at the very end of the list, the tool Benedict saves for last: never despair of God's mercy. Think about why that one comes last. A monk who's tried to use all the others will fail at some of them. Maybe most of them, on a bad day. The list seems to expect that. So the final tool is the one for when the rest have slipped out of your hands. Then Benedict names the workshop. The place where you use these tools, he says, is the enclosure of the monastery and staying put in the community. Not somewhere far off. Right where you already are. A long list, and one tool you never put down.
screen: `A LIST WITHOUT EXPLANATIONS.` · `KEEP DEATH BEFORE YOUR EYES.` · `THE LAST TOOL: NEVER DESPAIR.` · `THE WORKSHOP IS WHERE YOU ARE.` · then, large: `WITH THY WHOLE HEART.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: pick one tool. Settle, and breathe. Let a few of today's tools pass slowly through your mind. Love your neighbor as yourself. Make peace before the sun goes down. Pray for your enemies. Keep death before your eyes. Never despair of God's mercy. Notice which one your day actually needs. Not the most impressive one. The one that fits the job. Hold it for a while. If you pray, you can ask God for help using it well today. The bell holds the time.
The tools of good works. Chapter four of Benedict's Rule: a long list of short instructions for the inner life, ending with never despair of God's mercy. Today's word.
screen: `THE TOOLS OF GOOD WORKS — today's word`.

segments.voice: Your line: never despair. Today, use the one tool you picked, once. And if it slips, reach for the last tool on the board. Day one thousand one hundred ninety-one.

howItsDone: Benedictines read chapter 4 of the Rule in turn with the other chapters, and some readers use the list as an examination of conscience.

original.note: Latin, the last line of the Rule's list: never to despair of God's mercy.

trapdoor: what you thought: a monk's rulebook of dos and don'ts.
what it means: a pegboard of short tools for the inner life, used right where you are, ending with never despair.
what a scholar hears: instrumenta bonorum operum; the workshop, officina, is the cloister and stability in the community.

notes: Chapter 4 is paraphrased (Gasquet 1909 wording unverified); no count of tools is given. Confirm: the list opens with the two great commandments; includes 'mortem cotidie ante oculos suspectam habere', 'nihil amori Christi praeponere', 'pacem falsam non dare', peace before sundown, praying for enemies; closes with 'et de Dei misericordia numquam desperare'; the workshop is 'claustra monasterii et stabilitas in congregatione'.
'Some from the Ten Commandments, some from the Sermon on the Mount' describes sources of items in the list; confirm.
The reading of 'keep death before your eyes' as focusing rather than frightening is offered as the Rule's intent; confirm tone.
Editor pass: 'Benedict expects that' (attributing an intent the text doesn't state) softened to 'the list seems to expect that'; howItsDone's claim about keeping one tool 'for a season' softened.
